brief: BofA argues it is now a better time to revisit bonds after years as bond bears. Bonds are more attractive than the S&P 500 than at any point in 20+ years on earnings and dividend yield, and bond allocations sit at four-year lows. Valuation, a poor timing signal but a strong decade-ahead predictor, implies -3% annualized S&P 500 returns over the next decade against +3% for the average stock, which nets to a wash with a 2% dividend yield, so BofA still prefers stocks with positive gearing to growth over bonds and cash. Separately, BofA's rate strategists expect the 10yr and 2yr to settle at 5% by year-end, with upside risk to 5.5%+. Key equity thresholds: 5% is where investors turn indifferent between bonds and stocks, 6% is where stock-bond correlations go negative, and 7% is where PE multiples compress. Real Estate, Tech, Utilities and Communication Services carry the most negative rate sensitivity; Banks benefit from higher rates via asset sensitivity. S&P 500 leverage is healthier than prior cycles (80% of debt long-term fixed, up from 60% in 2007), with the debt burden now concentrated in government rather than corporate balance sheets.
